// diagnostic

E0035

An enum discriminant must be known at compile time and fit the signed integer representation used by the enum layout.

What

An enum discriminant must be known at compile time and fit the signed integer representation used by the enum layout.

Why

The enum number is part of the type layout, so it must be known before code generation.

Fix

Use an integer literal, a `NAME: comptime { value }` constant, or another compile-time expression that produces an in-range integer.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0035: tests/ui/cffi_enum_boundaries/cffi_enum_out_of_range_discriminant_stays_at_the_checked_boundary/stderr.

Error [jet.InvalidEnumDiscriminant]: An enum discriminant is outside the signed integer range
  --> tests/ui/cffi_enum_boundaries/cffi_enum_out_of_range_discriminant_stays_at_the_checked_boundary/run.jet:3:15
    |
  3 |     TooWide = 9223372036854775808
    |               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Enum discriminants are stored as signed 64-bit values
 Fix: Use a compile-time integer between -9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807
